Land & Water Conservation Fund

​​​LWCF provides federal grant funds to protect important natural areas, acquire land for outdoor recreation and to develop or renovate public outdoor recreation facilities such as campgrounds, picnic areas, sports & playfields, swimming facilities, boating facilities, fishing facilities, trails, natural areas and passive parks.

Who Can Apply: Cities, counties, state and federal agencies are eligible to apply for funding. The minimum amount is $25,000. The maximum grant amount is $1,000,000. It is a 50/50 matching reimbursement program.

Application Process: The 2026 application is available here. Applications are due on Friday, October 30, 2026. Please contact the office if you have any questions. ​​

Additional Requirements

  • You must submit to the State Clearinghouse for the Intergovernmental Review Process or request an update on previous comments to be eligible for funding.
  • All recreational facilities that have received LWCF assistance must stay outdoor recreational for perpetuity.
  • The land must be owned or be able to obtain a long term lease from a Public Agency. The Public Agency will have to agree in writing to keeping the land recreational in perpetuity if the lease expires.

Land Appraisals

Acquisition of land may be accomplished through purchase, transfer, gift or other means. All acquisitions must conform to the Uniform Relocation Assistance and Real Property Acquistiion Policies Act of 1970. Please see KYTC Pre-qualified Appraisers​​ list for an appraiser in your area.

All Land Appraisals must adhere to the Appraisal Requirements for the Commonwealth of Kentucky.​

Deed Restriction Requirement

All sponsors who receive a LWCF grant must file a separate deed restriction prior to receiving reimbursement.

LWCF Advisory Board Meeting Announcement

The next Land and Water Conservation Fund (LWCF) Advisory Board Meeting will be held Thursday, January 22, 2026, at 9:00 a.m. EST. During this meeting, board members will review 2025 LWCF applications and make funding recommendations. The meeting is open to the public.​

WHAT: Land and Water Conservation Fund Advisory Board Meeting
WHEN: Thursday, January 22, 2026 at 9:00 a.m. EST​​
WHERE: 100 Airport Rd. Frankfort, KY 40601. 3rd Floor. 

The LWCF is funded by the Department of the Interior’s National Park Service and administered by the Department for Local Government. Funding can be used for the acquisition of property and the development and/or renovation of public outdoor recreational facilities in the state of Kentucky. Outdoor recreational facilities include campgrounds, picnic areas, sports & playfields, swimming facilities, trails, passive parks, etc.​

If you have any questions, please feel free to contact the office.

Please submit all ​applications to the the office​.

SCORP (Statewide Comprehensive Outdoor Recreation Plan)

​SCORP Recertification — Public Comment Opportunity

The Kentucky Department for Local Government is pursuing a five-year recertification of the existing Statewide Comprehensive Outdoor Recreation Plan (SCORP).

As part of this process, DLG invites public input to ensure the current plan continues to reflect the outdoor recreation needs and priorities of Kentucky residents.

The public is encouraged to review the existing SCORP and submit comments regarding the proposed recertification by November 6th, 2026

Comments may be submitted to the office. 

Review the Current SCORP: KY SCORP
